units.oneLiner: Keep every key in the slot array itself and, when the home slot is taken, probe the next slot and the next: the probes stay inside the cache line the first one fetched, Knuth's 1963 formulas say exactly what each load factor costs, and the price is clustering, which is why the table resizes before it is full and why the hash must scatter neighbors.
units.description: Linear probing on 65,536 slots against Knuth's 1963 formulas (within 1% to load 0.7) and a Python set over 1,200,000 operations: at load 0.9 a hit costs 5.315 probes but 1.540 cache lines against 2.570 and 2.570 for double hashing; clusters of 715 slots; tombstones 5.864 probes per miss against 1.698 for backward shift; a weak hash costs 1,056 probes per hit.
units.time: O(1) expected; (1 + 1/(1 - a)) / 2 probes per hit

units.plan_row: Open addressing × Linear probing. Puzzle 172, data-structures (problemSlug hash-collision-resolution, the atlas problem page carrying "Cache-friendly hashing"; sibling live lesson cuckoo-hashing-two-table-eviction-kicks). Solution open_addressing_linear_probing.py (3.0s, prints OK): linear probing with tombstone or backward-shift deletion and a rebuild at 85% live-plus-tombstones, quadratic probing (triangular offsets), double hashing (odd stride), separate chaining, Robin Hood, Fibonacci and weak hashes, a probe-and-cache-line counter (8 slots per 64-byte line, one line per chaining node). ORACLES: (1) Knuth 1963 at loads 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.7 / 0.8 / 0.9 / 0.95: hits 1.164 / 1.509 / 2.172 / 3.027 / 5.962 / 11.609 against 1.167 / 1.500 / 2.167 / 3.000 / 5.500 / 10.500, misses 1.397 / 2.510 / 5.971 / 12.655 / 50.434 / 205.639 against 1.389 / 2.500 / 6.056 / 13.000 / 50.500 / 200.500 (within 6% to 0.8, 20% beyond); (2) 1,200,000 mixed operations across six structures all matching a Python set, final sizes matching; (3) the race at load 0.9 (every key looked up, 5,000 misses): linear probing 5.315 probes/hit, 47.975/miss, 1.540 lines/hit, variance 277, max 612, longest cluster 715; Robin Hood 5.315 / 5.644 / 1.540 / 19.8 / 29; quadratic 2.850 / 12.055 / 1.951 / 16.2 / 92; double hashing 2.570 / 10.056 / 2.570 / 11.1 / 68; chaining 2.450 / 1.923 / 2.450 / 0.5 / 9; longest run by load 8 / 31 / 85 / 209 / 752 / 3,250; (4) deletion: fill to 0.7, delete half: tombstones 5.864 probes per miss (formula for 0.7: 6.056), backward shift 1.698 (formula for 0.35: 1.683); (5) weak hash (high bits) on 2,048 consecutive keys in 4,096 slots: linear probing 1,056 probes per hit, double hashing 8.3, chaining 402.8, strong hash 1.50. Honest: linear probing pays twice double hashing's probes at 0.9 and wins only on lines; the Robin Hood mean is identical to 1e-9 (the displacement total is invariant), asserted; three author notes recorded (quadratic vs double ordering; the first weak-hash experiment at 65,536 slots ran quadratic for ten minutes and was shrunk; a 5,000-key hit sample was replaced by every key after the early-inserted keys biased it). Cards: self, Hash table with chaining, Robin Hood hashing, Cuckoo hashing (live lesson badge) (all algoName). neverUse: linear probing with a hash that keeps neighbors neighbors. Figure: Knuth's hit and miss curves with the measured points beside bars of the longest run by load; cite Knuth 1963 / TAOCP 3 6.4, Amdahl et al. 1954, Pagh-Pagh-Ruzic STOC 2007 DOI 10.1145/1250790.1250839. Viz LinearProbingViz: a 64-slot table as eight cache lines filling to load 0.9, walked slots amber and touched lines outlined, the running average probes per insert against Knuth's expectation, every key checked reachable from its home each tick; NODE-VERIFIED 20 cycles x 21 ticks, 0 breaks; stepMs 500, holdTicks rests. Preserved narration: Aoede + Algieba.

units.oneLiner: Take any tour, find two edges whose swap (reconnect a to c and b to d, reversing the path between them) is shorter, apply it, and repeat until a full pass finds none: in the plane every crossing is such a swap, so the local optimum is crossing-free, each test costs four distance lookups, and sorted neighbor lists make a pass near-linear.
units.description: 2-opt tour improvement against an exact Held-Karp referee on twenty 16-city instances: 1.85% above optimal from nearest neighbor (optimal 13 of 20), 0.00% with Or-opt; zero crossings at every local optimum from 16 to 1,600 cities; 400 cities untangled in 103 swaps and 46 ms; neighbor lists of twenty cut 40.9M lookups to 2.95M.
units.time: O(n²) per pass, O(nk) with neighbor lists, passes until one is clean
units.space: the tour and a position array
units.plan_row: 2-opt × Edge-uncrossing swaps. Puzzle 188, optimization-or (problemSlug traveling-salesman, the atlas problem page carrying "Tour improvement"; sibling live lessons annealing-cooling 2, held-karp-bitmask-states 81, christofides-matching-euler-tour 117). Solution two_opt_edge_uncrossing_swaps.py (13.3 s, prints OK): distance matrix, nearest neighbor, segment-intersection crossing counter, sorted neighbor lists, 2-opt (first- or best-improvement, full scan or Johnson-McGeoch neighbor-list candidates in both tour directions, shorter-side reversal), Or-opt (runs of 1 to 3, both orientations), Held-Karp bitmask DP, brute force. ORACLES: (1) Held-Karp equals brute force at n = 9; twenty random instances at n = 16, exact gap over the optimum: nearest neighbor mean 14.98% max 41.60% optimal 1/20; 2-opt from NN mean 1.85% max 8.31% optimal 13/20; 2-opt then Or-opt 0.00% optimal 20/20; 2-opt from random mean 4.12% max 17.93% optimal 8/20; crossings over the 20 instances NN 30, random 491, every 2-opt local optimum 0; Held-Karp total 3.5 s; (2) zero crossings at every full-neighborhood local optimum at n = 100, 200, 400, 800, 1,600 (NN starts had 17 / 24 / 32 / 62 / 147 crossings, random starts 1,026 / 5,068 / 18,278 / 69,376), every accepted delta negative and the deltas summing to the length change, every tour a permutation; (3) n = 400 (BHH estimate 14.25): NN 18.472 (1.296x), 79,800 lookups, 32 crossings; 2-opt full scan 16.241 (1.140x) 1,369,560 lookups 103 moves 46 ms 0 crossings; neighbor lists k=10 15.802, 185,618 lookups, 110 moves, 17 ms, 0 crossings; k=20 15.802, 186,230, 110 moves, 18 ms, 0; 2-opt then Or-opt 15.664 (1.099x) +3,824,750 lookups +41 moves 138 ms; random tour 203.411 (14.276x) 18,278 crossings; 2-opt from random 16.766 (1.177x) 2,223,069 lookups 2,334 moves 78 ms; n = 1,600: NN 36.930 (147 crossings); full scan 31.579 (1.108x) 40,919,705 lookups 523 moves 1,927 ms 0 crossings; k=10 31.254, 3,086,785 lookups, 5 crossings; k=20 31.010, 2,951,243 lookups, 304 ms, 0 crossings; n = 800: full 22.225 / k=20 22.038 / Or-opt 21.623 / from random 23.156 in 5,700 moves; (4) first vs best improvement, n = 100, ten instances, means: NN first 8.291 (79,192 lookups, 36 moves), NN best 8.171 (298,860, 19), random first 8.561 (112,941, 401), random best 8.362 (1,519,205, 103). Honest: AUTHOR CORRECTIONS recorded in the file: the draft expected neighbor lists of ten to lose nothing (they left 5 crossings at n = 1,600; twenty was clean at every size for a seventh to a fourteenth of the lookups), expected first and best improvement to tie (best is 1.4% / 2.3% shorter at 3.8x / 13.5x the lookups), and the neighbor-list scan landed on a shorter local optimum than the full scan at every size (a different path, not a bigger neighborhood). Cards: self (2-opt), Or-opt, Lin-Kernighan, Simulated annealing (live lesson badge, puzzle 2) (all algoName, all pages in dist/algo). neverUse: Held-Karp or any exact search at n = 400 (0.18 s per 16-city instance, doubling per city, 2^400 states). Figure: the uncrossing geometry (red removed pair, amber added pair, the triangle inequality at the crossing point X) beside a bar chart of the exact gaps at n = 16 with optimal counts; cite Croes 1958 Operations Research DOI 10.1287/opre.6.6.791, Flood 1956, Johnson and McGeoch 1997. Viz TwoOptViz: 2-opt from a seeded random tour of 13 cities, one swap per two ticks (show the red removed pair and amber dashed added pair, then apply), crossing pairs taken first then the remaining improving swaps, the exact Held-Karp optimum computed in makeScene as an amber tick on the length bar, invariant every swap: permutation, strict descent by exactly the predicted delta, never below the optimum, zero crossings at the local optimum; NODE-VERIFIED 20 cycles x 30.4 ticks (max 54), 0 breaks, gaps 0% to 7.4% across cycles; stepMs 280, holdTicks rests. units.oneLiner: Seal the bids, give the item to the highest, and charge the second bid: your bid then decides only whether you win, never what you pay, so the truth is a dominant strategy, the highest value always wins, and the seller earns exactly what a first-price auction would at equilibrium, without anyone computing one.
units.description: The Vickrey auction against exhaustive deviation checks and closed forms: 0 profitable deviations in 4,029,261 comparisons; the highest value wins 60,000 of 60,000 draws; revenue 0.4997 at n = 3 against first-price 0.4994 and theory 0.5; Myerson's reserve 0.5 lifts two-bidder revenue from 0.333 to 0.418; a seller shill steals 0.2496 per sale.
units.time: O(n log n) to sort the bids, O(n) with two running maxima
units.plan_row: Vickrey auction × Second-price rule. Puzzle 189, optimization-or (problemSlug auction-design, the atlas problem page carrying "Truthful single-item auction"; sibling live lessons gale-shapley-deferred-acceptance, puzzle 73, and secretary-one-over-e). Solution vickrey_auction_second_price_rule.py (0.76s, prints OK): a Vickrey auction with optional reserve, a first-price auction, an ascending clock auction, second-price and first-price payoff functions, the expected first-price payoff against equilibrium rivals, the closed-form two-bidder reserve revenue 1/3 + r^2 - 4r^3/3, and a mean with standard error. ORACLES, i.i.d. uniform [0, 1] values, 60,000 draws per cell: (1) dominant strategy exhaustively: 21 values x 21 highest rival bids x 21 deviations = 9,261 grid comparisons plus 20,000 random continuous profiles x 201 deviations = 4,020,000, total 4,029,261 comparisons, 0 profitable deviations from the truth; under a first-price rule 210 of the 441 grid (value, rival) cells reward shading; (2) first-price equilibrium by best response: against rivals bidding (n - 1)v/n, the best reply on a 1,000-bid grid is within 0.0007 of (n - 1)v/n over n = 2, 3, 5 and v = 0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0, and bidding v earns exactly 0 (equilibrium utility 0.149 on average); (3) revenue equivalence: Vickrey 0.3351 +/- 0.0010, 0.4997 +/- 0.0009, 0.6665 +/- 0.0007 at n = 2, 3, 5 against first-price at equilibrium 0.3340 +/- 0.0005, 0.4994 +/- 0.0005, 0.6668 +/- 0.0005 and theory (n - 1)/(n + 1) = 0.3333, 0.5, 0.6667, all within three standard errors; the highest value won 60,000 of 60,000 at every n; an ascending clock at increment 0.001 matched the Vickrey winner on 3,000 of 3,000 draws and the price within 0.001, 500 rounds per auction on average; (4) Myerson's reserve: the closed form peaks at r = 0.500 on a 1,000-point grid; simulated two-bidder revenue 0.3330 +/- 0.0010 (r = 0, formula 0.3333), 0.3859 +/- 0.0008 (0.3, formula 0.3873), 0.4181 +/- 0.0010 (0.5, formula 0.4167), 0.3674 +/- 0.0015 (0.7, formula 0.3660), each within three standard errors, 0.5 the best; unsold 0%, 9.2%, 24.7%, 48.8%; (5) efficiency and the negative example: Vickrey misallocates on 0 of 60,000 draws; a first-price auction between a bidder shading by half and one shading by a fifth misallocates 18.7% of draws and loses 3.5% of welfare; a seller who reads the bids and shills just under the winner extracts 0.2496 +/- 0.0008 per sale at n = 3, the whole gap E[v1 - v2] = 1/(n + 1) = 0.25. Author correction recorded (the draft called the two-bidder reserve gain a third; the formula gives 1/3 to 5/12, a quarter). Cards: self, VCG mechanism, Myerson optimal auction, Ascending clock auction (all algoName; pages verified in dist/algo). neverUse: the second-price rule with a seller who can read the bids (the shill) or colluding bidders. Figure: payoff against bid for a bidder with value 0.8 facing a rival bid of 0.5 under both rules (the second-price step, flat above the rival, truth optimal; first-price 0.8 - b, truth earns 0) beside the two-bidder revenue curve against the reserve with four measured points peaking at 0.5; cite Vickrey 1961 Journal of Finance DOI 10.1111/j.1540-6261.1961.tb02789.x, Myerson 1981, Clarke 1971, Groves 1973. Viz VickreyViz: sixty three-bidder sealed-bid auctions, one per tick, bars for the bids with the winner green and the amber second-price line, a probed bidder's payoff-against-bid step curve, running Vickrey and equilibrium first-price revenue against (n - 1)/(n + 1) = 0.5; invariant every tick: the highest value wins, pays the second value, and 41 probed deviations never beat the truth; NODE-VERIFIED 20 cycles x 60 ticks, 0 breaks (2,460 deviations per cycle); stepMs 420, holdTicks rests. units.oneLiner: Scan the pixels once in reading order, giving each foreground pixel the label of a neighbor already seen or a fresh one, record every meeting of two labels as a union, then rewrite each label to its root in a second pass: two streaming reads, no stack, no recursion, and a merge-only table sized by labels, not pixels.
units.description: Two-pass labeling against a flood-fill referee: equal partitions on 88 image-connectivity pairs; 38,400 visits (two per pixel) against 41,280 and 63,360; 179 and 78 provisional labels for 28 and 27 blobs merged by 151 and 51 unions at 0.635 and 0.405 links per find; a 3,220-pixel snake crashes a recursive fill; the naive single pass splits every U.
units.time: O(n α(n)): two passes over n pixels, near-constant per union and find
units.space: O(L) parent and rank entries for L provisional labels, plus the label image
units.baseline: Breadth-first flood fill from every unlabeled pixel
units.plan_row: Connected component labeling × Two-pass union-find. Puzzle 190, signal-graphics (problemSlug region-labeling, the atlas problem page carrying "Region labeling"; sibling live lessons canny-edge-detector-hysteresis-thresholding, puzzle 173, and unionfind-rank-compression, puzzle 8). Solution connected_component_labeling_two_pass_union_find.py (0.3s, prints OK): a counting union-find (unions, finds, parent links followed) with path compression and union by rank, the two-pass labeler (visits, provisional labels), an iterative BFS flood fill (visits, queue maximum), a recursive flood fill (max depth, RecursionError reported instead of crashing), run-length labeling, union-find over raw pixels, the naive single pass, and image builders (random disks, separated disks, a one-pixel-wide snake, U shapes, diagonal stripes). ORACLES: (1) partition equality (never label numbers) against the BFS on a 160 x 120 image of 60 disks (5,520 foreground pixels) under 4- and 8-connectivity, on 40 random 64 x 48 images under both (80 pairs), and on 10, 25, and 40 separated disks whose counts are known by construction: 88 comparisons, with run-length labeling and pixel union-find agreeing too; (2) counts: 28 / 27 components; two-pass 38,400 visits (exactly 2 per pixel, asserted) against BFS 41,280 / 63,360 (queue max 30 / 50); provisional labels 179 / 78, unions 151 / 51, finds 7,934 / 7,474 at 0.635 / 0.405 links per find (asserted under 1.5); unions == sets made minus components asserted for every method; run-length 499 runs, 471 / 472 unions, 1,443 / 1,455 finds; pixel union-find 5,520 sets, 5,492 / 5,493 unions, 25,588 / 45,026 finds at 0.824 / 0.889 links; recursive fill 41,280 / 63,360 visits (equal to BFS, asserted), depth 597 / 573; (3) snake 160 x 40 (3,220 pixels, one component): two-pass 12,800 visits, 11 labels, 10 unions; BFS queue max 1; recursive fill depth 3,220 at limit 50,000 and RecursionError at the default 1,000 (asserted); (4) diagonal stripes 60 x 60 period 3: 1,200 components under 4-connectivity (every pixel alone), 39 under 8 (asserted against the stripe count); (5) negative example: naive single pass 60 labels for 30 U shapes (asserted at least 2 per U) and 78 for 27 blobs under 8-connectivity; the two-pass made the same 60 provisional labels and 30 unions on the U image. Honest: author correction recorded (the draft expected about one provisional label per component; measured several per blob, 179 for 28 under 4-connectivity, because every row where a blob widens on its left starts a label). Cards: self, Flood fill, Union-find (live lesson badge, puzzle 8), Run-length encoding (all algoName; pages verified in dist/algo). neverUse: one raster pass with no equivalence table (60 labels for 30 U shapes), with the recursive flood fill crash as its cousin. Figure: pass one on a U shape with labels 1 and 2 and the amber union at the corner, beside a log-scale chart of sets made and finds spent (two-pass 78 / 7,474; run-length 499 / 1,455; pixel union-find 5,520 / 45,026); cite Rosenfeld and Pfaltz JACM 1966 DOI 10.1145/321356.321357, He, Chao, Suzuki IEEE TIP 2008, Wu, Otoo, Suzuki PAA 2009. Viz ComponentLabelingViz: a seeded 48 x 16 image (disks, two U shapes, specks) under 4- or 8-connectivity per cycle; pass one six pixels per tick with provisional-label colors and an amber flash per union, pass two twelve per tick recoloring to final components; invariant every tick of pass one: the union-find classes over the scanned prefix equal an independent flood fill's components of that prefix; at the end partition equality with the full flood fill, visits == 2N, unions == labels minus components; NODE-VERIFIED 20 cycles x 191 ticks, 0 breaks; stepMs 60, holdTicks rests. units.oneLiner: Count each symbol, divide by n, and plug the frequencies into Shannon's formula: one pass, nothing to tune, and a bias that is always negative and known to first order, (k − 1)/(2n ln 2) bits, so that at ten samples per symbol one added term makes it honest and at one sample per symbol nothing does.
units.description: The plug-in entropy estimator against its exact expectation: bias −0.0728 bits at n = 1,000 for 100 equiprobable symbols (Miller −0.0714), −0.00715 at 10,000, −3.41 at n = 10; Miller-Madow and the jackknife erase it at n ≫ k; a 2,000-symbol tail at n = 2,000 sits 0.583 bits low; independent variables show 0.0587 bits of plug-in mutual information.
units.time: O(n + k) per estimate: one pass over the samples, one over the counts
units.baseline: Compressed size per symbol (Huffman on the counts)
units.plan_row: Shannon entropy estimation × Maximum likelihood plug-in. Puzzle 195, compression-coding (problemSlug entropy-estimation, the atlas problem page carrying "Entropy estimation"; sibling live lesson huffman-frequency-merges). Solution shannon_entropy_estimation_maximum_likelihood_plug_in.py (0.7 s, prints OK, 62 assertions): the plug-in in its log n form, Miller-Madow and jackknife corrections, the EXACT expectation of the plug-in as a sum of binomial terms (a brute force over every count vector on a 4-symbol alphabet at n = 8 agrees to 1e-12: 1.532790 bits against a truth of 1.846439), a Huffman coder on the counts, Zipf distributions, and a plug-in mutual information. ORACLES: (1) 100 equiprobable symbols (6.644 bits): exact bias -3.41 at n = 10 (E[plug-in] 3.233, log2 10 = 3.322), -2.01 at 30, -0.822 at 100 (Miller first-order -0.714), -0.261 at 300, -0.0728 at 1,000 (-0.0714), -0.0239 at 3,000, -0.00715 at 10,000 (-0.00714); Miller-Madow -2.79, -1.40, -0.370, -0.034, -0.0012 (exact -0.00136), -0.0001, -0.0000; jackknife -2.12, -0.83, -0.065, +0.027, +0.0018, +0.0002, -0.0000; sd 0.0101 at 1,000 and 0.0009 at 10,000 (ratio 11.06: the uniform leading variance term vanishes, 1/n). (2) Zipf over 100 symbols (5.310 bits): bias -2.43 at n = 10, -0.663 at 100, -0.0765 at 1,000 (sd 0.0738), -0.0072 at 10,000 (sd 0.0217; ratio 3.40 against root ten 3.16); Miller-Madow -0.0104 and jackknife +0.0031 at 1,000. (3) All 14 Monte Carlo means (120 to 200 reps) within 3 standard errors of the exact expectation, for the plug-in and for Miller-Madow; bias ratios 1,000 against 10,000: 10.17 uniform, 10.66 Zipf; no sample above log2 of the symbols seen (2,480 samples). (4) Code length on a Zipf sample of 10,000: plug-in 5.2808 = ideal code length; Huffman 5.3185; truth 5.3102. (5) Independent 10 x 10 variables, n = 1,000, 300 reps: plug-in mutual information 0.0587 +/- 0.0005 bits, exact expectation 0.0598, first order (kx - 1)(ky - 1)/(2n ln 2) = 0.0584. (6) NEGATIVE EXAMPLE: Zipf over 2,000 symbols (8.115 bits) at n = 2,000: 632 symbols ever seen, plug-in -0.583, Miller-Madow -0.356, jackknife -0.205; at n = 20,000: -0.079, -0.015, +0.005, 1,785 seen. AUTHOR CORRECTION recorded: the draft claimed the spread shrinks like 1/sqrt(n) for every distribution; the uniform case shrinks like 1/n. Cards: self, Miller-Madow correction, Jackknife resampling (Zahl's entropy jackknife), NSB entropy estimator (all algoName pages exist). neverUse: the plug-in reported as unbiased when n is of the order of k. Figure: exact bias curves (plug-in, Miller's formula, Miller-Madow, jackknife) on log axes beside the collapse bars at n = 10 to 1,000 with the log2 n ceiling; cite Shannon 1948 (DOI 10.1002/j.1538-7305.1948.tb01338.x), Miller 1955, Paninski 2003 (DOI 10.1162/089976603321780272), Nemenman-Shafee-Bialek 2002. Viz EntropyEstimationViz: a seeded 8-to-16-symbol source, the sample growing 15% per tick to 2,000, empirical bars against true outlines, the plug-in and Miller-Madow climbing toward the truth on a log n axis with the gap shaded; invariants per tick (two formula forms agree, estimate <= log2 of symbols seen, non-negative, correction >= raw); NODE-VERIFIED 20 cycles, 44 ticks each, 0 breaks; stepMs 350, holdTicks rests.
